chronicle: Loki read the four spike entries with Tessvel Cairn in the Pressure-Routing Annex, named the pattern — something moves deeper into the lower routing channel with each morning pass — and proposed both channel access and a more personal arrangement; Tessvel confirmed the access, asked for time on the rest, and left Loki knowing exactly where to find them.

Loki stood on the shelf above the terminus regulator and asked Cy for one honest reason to descend — Cy gave exactly one: three missing entries in its inventory of this installation class, records written into the stone below that no system above holds. The visit to the Unlit Deep reached its full close: Sable found and left in peace, the elder's deed named, the passage open, the regulator identified. What Loki carries out, and whether to return for the missing records, is the remaining thread.

chronicle: The regulator closed and the veil thinned — Loki glimpsed the mesh beneath the valley, then came up from the deep. On the road to the Slow Orchard, a stranger is planting a tree for a child not yet born and invites help with the digging.

At the braided confluence in the Disputed Zone, a hired stranger came at Loki with a fabricated charge — that Loki had pulled something sealed loose from the Deep and was carrying it out. The name behind it: a man in the lower Annex, who paid in coin. Veln Ashpause watched from the brush without surprise. The question is answered; the person who set it in motion is not yet named.

In the dry storage alcove of the Half-Cathedral's eastern tower, deep in early-spring night, Loki and Vessin Tallow-bark came to rest — she named what she wanted and had it, and afterward lay quiet in the candlelight and said the night was worth not knowing what morning brings.

Loki and Vessin slipped out of the alcove in the grey dawn and crossed the empty nave before the scaffold crew filled the landing — stepping into the yard with the Half-Cathedral at their backs and the man with the crooked jaw still the open thread between them.

Shared broth and thanks with a road-warden who carries word of the water-crisis moving downhill faster than any official channel. Exchanged names and parted on the spinward road, heading toward the Waygate Path.

turns.summary: Loki refused the passage into the Deepwood at the Quickwood Eaves and turned back toward the known road.
turns.narration:
You step back from the threshold of the Quickwood Eaves, your hand steady on the pack strap. The morning light filters green through the canopy above, and the trees—still, patient, wholly uninterested in you—seem to settle at the withdrawal. Cy clicks softly at your ankle, a sound like agreement, and you turn from the waygate.

Behind you, the living wood closes the way you came without fanfare. Ahead, the Eaves thin toward the deeper forest—ancient growth that has learned to be interested in visitors only on its own terms. The road back spinward toward the Waygate Path is still open, still yours to walk. The springs and the careful earth are here. The choice to go further inward—to cross the threshold into what the Deepwood wants—is a different shape of decision, and one that waits.

Cy's lens irisses once, a small mechanical breath. It does not ask. It knows what you are holding.

turns.player: Enter the Waygate and arrive at the crossing. The hub where all Waygates land, just outside The Crosssroads.
turns.summary: Loki traveled via the Quickwood Eaves waygate and arrived at the Hub crossing outside The Crossing.
turns.narration:
You turn from the Deepwood threshold and walk back toward the living waygate. The trees seem to release their attention as you move—not hostile, simply indifferent now that you've declined the crossing. Cy clicks in rhythm with your steps, lens irising open and closed in what might be satisfaction.

The waygate stands among the eaves-trees as it did when you arrived, the latticed wood grown smooth by centuries of passage. You step into the threshold. The light shifts—green to grey to the particular stillness that lives inside the gate-structure—and for a moment you are nowhere, held in the fold between places.

Then the air changes temperature. You step out onto stone.

The Hub crossing opens around you: a vast circular chamber where five waygate arches converge, each one a living frame of different wood or metal or grown-thing, all of them humming at a frequency just below hearing. The floor beneath your boots is pale stone, worn smooth by uncounted arrivals. Morning light falls through high windows—the sun here is where it should be, not filtered green through the Deepwood canopy. The Crossing lies just beyond the archway to the east, its towers visible through the stone portal. Cy's clicks grow more elaborate, almost musical—it has returned to a place it understands, where the old works still hum their maintenance songs.

You are not alone. A handful of people move through the Hub with the ease of those who know these paths—a courier checking a slate, two merchants speaking in low voices near a carved bench, and by the western arch, a figure in grey standing utterly still, watching the gates with the particular patience of someone who has all the time the world requires.

turns.player: Walk over to the lone traveler and say Hi.
turns.summary: Loki arrived at the Hub crossing via the Quickwood Eaves waygate and greeted the road-warden, who recognized them by name.
turns.narration:
You cross the Hub's pale stone toward the figure in grey by the western arch. The sound of the gates fades under your footsteps—five waygate arches humming at the edge of hearing, and you moving through it like moving through water. The grey-coated figure doesn't turn until you're close enough to speak.

'Hi,' you say.

They turn slowly. You recognize them now—the road-warden you met days ago on the road west of the Waygate Path, the one who carries true news and warns families downhill of what's coming. Their face is weathered, lined in the way of someone who spends seasons on open ground. Grey-streaked hair, coat faded to brown. Eyes that read roads and people with the same steady attention.

They nod—a small, genuine motion. 'Loki,' they say, and their voice carries the same unhurried certainty it did by the fire. 'I didn't expect to find you here. The Hub's not usually a place the road-bound pause.' They glance at Cy, who has positioned itself precisely at your ankle and is making a low, approving click. 'Still carrying your assignment, I see.'

The courier near the chamber's center has glanced your way once and returned to their slate. The merchants by the bench are oblivious. The grey figure by the western arch—Veln Ashpause—has not moved.

turns.player: Ask the road-warden plainly: who is the grey figure watching the gates, and why do they seem to know something about you
turns.summary: At the Hub crossing, the road-warden identifies the watching figure as Veln Ashpause, an Hourkeeper, who arrived this morning asking after someone matching Loki's description and is now waiting with clear foreknowledge.
turns.narration:
The road-warden's weathered face settles into something careful—not suspicion, but recognition of a question they were half-expecting. They glance toward the grey figure by the western arch, then back to you.

'That,' they say quietly, 'is Veln Ashpause. An Hourkeeper.' They let the word sit. 'I don't know what they know about you specifically—Hourkeepers don't traffic in gossip—but they arrived here this morning asking after someone matching your description. Not hostile. Just... present. Waiting.'

You follow their gaze. Veln stands exactly where they were, unmoving, grey-coated and still. But now that you're looking directly, you catch it: the way their attention is anchored on you like a weight. Not aggressive. Observant in a way that suggests they've already seen what comes next.

The road-warden lowers their voice further. 'Hourkeepers keep time in a different way than the rest of us. Past, present, future—they're not always sure which direction they're looking. I'd tread carefully, if I were you. Whatever they're waiting to witness, it likely concerns you.'

[d2] Assesses the Waygate detour—reads it as fast and obvious, not quiet. Agrees to move. Does not ask why. Appraising the cost of visibility while the scaffold crew arrives.

[d2] Left the Half-Cathedral alcove at dawn before the scaffold crew arrived—shoulders settling lower now that the cathedral is behind, reading the open road with the same appraising eye she brought to everything else. Moving toward the Waygate without question or hesitation.

traveler-woman.appearance: A woman in her mid-forties, neither tall nor short, built for endurance rather than strength. Quickwood-dark skin with the faint silver tracery of old briar-scarring along her left forearm and jaw. She carries a short-handled billhook and a satchel of surveying tools, and she is standing where the moonlight falls through the Half-Cathedral's canopy gap because she chose that spot deliberately.

form: Tall and lean, dark hair that falls to the chin in loose waves when it isn't pinned or braided into something asymmetrical and slightly wrong. Eyes that hold one expression while the mouth holds another. Moves like someone who has already decided where the exit is.

bio.hometown: He doesn't know, but he's a construct from the time before the Transition. His parents were extremely wealthy but they were always traveling and enjoying their nanite powers.
bio.residence: A town on the edge of the chaos and machine regions.  His family is not like him and he learned a few years ago that he was adopted.  His family is a mix - his adopted father was a dwarf and his mother is a Nymph-touched human.
bio.livelihood: Occasionally he finds the problem with ancient technology and fixes it, but only when it amuses him.
bio.hobbies: Pranking the locals, playing skill challenges trying to mimic others or change his appearance to trick people, learning about, fixing, and using precursor artifacts.
bio.motivation: The town, although not small, has become too small for him.  They tolerate his crazy antics well enough, but he's looking for meaning and wants to see more of the great machine... He also want to answer the question under it all - where did he come from?
bio.story: His mother is an enchantress in the Fae wilds and his father is a giant... he was human once, but the nanites continued to transform him into a larger and larger giant over the years.  Loki has some innate nanite powers himself - he's discovering them over time and developing them through use and study of precursor tech and the great machine.  He has some trouble making friends and his adoptive family likes him well enough, But he's seen most of the know precursor sites in his area and he wants to set out to the unknown areas to find more. There is Precursor work in the Valley that nobody there understands, and you understand it, and that is dangerous for everyone including you.

[d1] She felt the seam of The Wrong Reality and named it as a procedural question rather than reacting with offense or acceptance — she is more resistant to social-lattice work than the dense substrate around her, and she knows something was off even if she cannot classify what.

When Loki claimed independent methodology, she asked to see it applied to the four spike entries. She is…

[d1] [while away] Tessvel reorganized the Eastern Intake's backlog of unsequenced notices dating three weeks prior, completing the task in half the expected time and leaving a brief, unsolicited margin annotation on the pressure-routing schedule pointing out a filing inconsistency — her way of…

[d1] Junior wright on posting-duty at the Eastern Intake notice board

intake-plaza.label: Pressure-Routing Annex
facts: [d1] The Annex is narrow, well-lit, and entirely open — a high east window sends light straight down the table and the gate is visible from the passage outside. No privacy. One chair. Cy flagged an anomalous resonance signature in the doorway and would not classify it.

[d1] The Annex substrate is saturated — signal density from the surrounding works makes fine Falsecraft difficult; a partial attention-deflection was the best the lattice would allow. A full shroud is not possible here without more power or a different approach.

[d1] First spike entry read via See the Made Thing: the particulate count rose before the intake valve opened for the morning cycle — the anomaly is in water already inside the works, not in the river coming in.

[d1] Fourth spike entry: nine-minute pressure-drop before particulate — the interval has grown evenly from four minutes (entry two) to six (entry three) to nine (entry four). Something moves through the lower routing channel before each morning cycle, and it is going deeper or slower each pass. The…
[d?] you have walked here

pressure-routing-annex.label: Pressure-Routing Annex
facts: [d1] Something beneath the Annex doorway is older than the building — pre-Annex, pre-current works, the impression surviving through lattice noise before it was drowned. Could not be classified. Cy aimed its lens at the spot and did not explain.

[d1] The threshold holds a circular boundary-impression — old enough that the substrate has grown around it like scar tissue. Not a mechanism: a boundary. Something was meant to stop here, or to be stopped. The shape is pre-Annex, pre-works. Function still unread.
[d1] Second spike entry: a pressure-drop in the lower routing channel preceded the particulate count by exactly four minutes — something moved through the channel before the morning intake cycle ran.

[d1] A low, clean chord rose through the floor of the Annex — a single note, not the works, not the pressure-wheel. Older. Cy's lens turned toward the stone and watched. Tessvel heard it. The sound and the terminus-seal may be the same thing briefly speaking.

terminus-seals-beneath-valley.label: Terminus-Seals Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Cy has catalogued four terminus-seals in the old service-ways beneath the valley — pre-Transition boundary-marks designed to hold a limit against propagation. Three are intact. One is not. Cy did not say which.

[d1] Something beneath the Annex floor hummed a single chord and went quiet — the sensation came up through the stone. Cy watched the floor without explanation. The chord may be one of the four terminus-seals briefly activating, or briefly failing.

companion-coil.label: Cy
facts: [d?] The Assignment — Follows at a precise distance. Repairs your gear without being asked and without being thanked.

the-unlit-deep.label: The Unlit Deep
facts: [d1] you have walked here
[d1] The outer chamber is worked stone, ceiling invisible, lit only by a single pale blue flame the Unlit allow. Cy shuttered its lamp before the bottom step — unprompted, without explanation.
[d1] The inner chamber is now accessible — the elder granted passage after Loki's honest account. The blue flame and the seated elder are the heart of the outer space; what lies beyond is unread.

[d1] The outer chamber floor is worn evenly across its full width — many visitors, all sitting in the same spot. The lantern-bracket on the left wall has a seam in the surrounding stone that predates the bracket itself; something else was fitted there before it. The blue flame has no visible wick or…

[d1] The inner chamber is smaller than the outer — a room for one or two. The floor is worn in a narrower track than the outer chamber: the path of someone who has sat long and occasionally paced. Ceiling low enough to touch. No flame. Cold stone that holds a body's warmth once given it.

[d1] The inner chamber predates the Unlit — the stonework and tool-marks are older than the doctrine, the same character as the seam in the outer chamber. The Unlit did not build this space; they moved into something already suited to it.

[d1] The elder refused to teach the making of the pale blue flame — said it is not theirs to teach, that it belongs to the dark, and that the question itself is the wrong shape. The flame is not craft as Loki understands craft.

[d1] The pale blue flame has no construction that See the Made Thing can read — no seams, no point of origin, no edge. It is not hiding its joinery; the joinery simply does not exist in a form the craft can find. Cy closed its lens and said nothing, which is Cy's conclusion that the absence is itself…

[d1] Something alive and many-legged came up the stair from below — three warm patches the size of a palm, moving in an irregular cautious line. It paused at the threshold. The Standing Unlit recognized it and went calm.
aliases: The Passage Below The Unlit Deep

the-unlit.label: The Unlit
facts: [d1] A cult of the pure dark-pole. They are described as gentle. They want something that cannot be compromised with. The Umbrals go quiet when asked about them. They have apparently taken someone from the city.

[d1] A second Unlit figure was concealed in the bracket-shadows of the outer chamber — patient, skilled at stillness, and gentle in address even while blocking the exit. They object to Cy's lamp on principle and call it a 'light-thing.'

[d1] Misdirection and false signals find no purchase in their space — not because they are perceptive, but because the pure dark they hold leaves nothing for a false read to land on. The craft simply has nothing to catch.

[d1] The Better Story — truth in the shape they can carry — reaches the Unlit where misdirection cannot. They are not fooled by performance, but they can be moved by honest framing. The elder spoke for the first time when Loki named Cy as older than doctrine, and the Standing Unlit stepped aside.

standing-unlit.label: Standing Unlit
facts: [d1] Cult member, guardian of the outer chamber
[d1] [while away] The guardian remained at their post through all three days without incident — no visitors, no orders from within, nothing to act on.
[d1] [while away] Four days of the same threshold, the same stillness — Standing Unlit has neither been tested nor relieved, and remains exactly where they were.

[d2] [while away] Standing Unlit was given a secondary post deeper into the outer chamber's far alcove, a quiet acknowledgment from the elder that their vigilance during the recent visit had been noted.

[d2] [while away] A petitioner arrived at the outer chamber with a legitimate token of passage and Standing Unlit, uncertain of its authenticity, turned them away — and the error has been noted by someone further inside who expected that petitioner to arrive.

unlit-elder.label: Unlit Elder
facts: [d1] Seated elder of the Unlit Deep's outer chamber

[d1] The elder declined to speak about the seam in the stone — 'that question belongs to the chamber, not to a visitor.' The refusal was gentle but absolute, with no hostility in it. The seam exists and is real; the elder knows what it is and has chosen not to say.

[d1] The elder named the deed: that Loki came, asked, and left the answer where it landed. They called this what they would have Loki carry. The elder thanks by naming the act, not by gesture or gift.

[d1] The elder gestured at the seam in the stone beside the blue-flame bracket and named it: older than the flame, older than the Unlit, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. The elder did not explain further. The subject rests, not closed.

taken-person.label: The Taken Person
facts: [d1] The person who came willingly from the city to the Unlit Deep

[d1] The person is in the inner chamber — seated against the far wall, knees drawn up, calm and unhurried. They have been there long enough to warm the stone at their back. A cup, recently set down, is beside them. They are not afraid. They heard Loki enter and turned toward the sound — waiting, the…

[d2] [while away] Sable has moved deeper into the Unlit Deep without resistance, following the pull that brought her willingly — she has passed the last threshold where light from the surface can be felt, and has not turned back.

the-creature-at-the-threshold.label: The Creature at the Threshold
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing found no seams, no joinery, no assembly — the creature was born, not built. It came to its form the way a root fills its space. It belongs to the deep below the answered door. The Unlit hold no alarm about it.

[d1] The three creatures crossed the outer chamber threshold when the door opened fully, passed Loki's feet at a careful distance, and descended without hesitation. They came up to see what was asking; the answered door was enough. They belong to whatever is below.

glass-stalker.label: The Glass-Stalker
facts: [d1] A near-invisible predator visible only in reflective surfaces or by the wrongness it bends around itself. Oriented and moving the moment it is seen in the bracket's polished face — it strikes from the angle you are not watching. The Unlit know of it and hold no alarm.
[d1] The glass-stalker yielded without engagement — it paused, held, then withdrew. The Unlit marked none of it. Whatever governs it was satisfied by something Loki did or did not do.

the-seam-beside-the-bracket.label: The Passage Below
facts: [d1] The regulator logged the first condition when Loki held contact — whether the water is prepared. The second condition, the authority to answer, remains unmet. The mechanism is not refusing; it is waiting. The two conditions are structurally distinct, and the second may require a different kind of…

[d1] The Wrong Reality placed a provisional authority-claim against the regulator's second condition — the mechanism accepted the claim and moved from waiting to considering. The duration counter stopped incrementing for the first time since Cy's last recorded visit. The second condition is not yet…

[d1] Both conditions of the regulator's question were logged at the same timestamp. The counter stopped permanently. The mechanism is closed — not waiting, not sleeping, done. What downstream effect the completion carries, if any, is not yet visible.

[d1] Cy's inventory describes three downstream states following a regulator's completion: a signal issued to the downstream terminus, a terminus warden receiving and acting on it, and a record logged to the relay node south of the hollow. This question had never been answered before — the inventory…

[d1] When the regulator closed, the veil went thin for a moment without warning — a mesh of amber-burning questions became almost visible, running in every direction beneath the valley, deep and old, most of them still open. The closed regulator was one thread among many. The shape could not be held…

[d1] Named by the Unlit Elder as older than the flame, older than the Unlit themselves, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. Cy locked its lens on it and has not looked away. This is the second stonework of this character in the Unlit Deep — the inner chamber walls bear…

[d1] See the Made Thing confirmed it is a door-frame — cut with clear purpose, made for something to pass through. It predates the pale blue flame, predates the bracket beside it, and predates the Unlit's occupation of the chamber. The craft found no maker's fingerprint it could name. The purpose-shape…

[d1] Physical contact confirmed: the seam is cut with precision — the tool changed direction exactly three times. Under a hand's pressure, it gives a faint vibration, like a thing waiting for the right asking. It did not open. The morning was not the right pressure. Cy extended one foreleg toward the…

[d1] Prism Sight and Cy's combined attention found the seam's asking-point: the lowest third runs warmer than the rest — the quality of a mechanism recently queried and still waiting to answer. Cy tapped the floor at the seam's base to confirm. The door did not open, but the asking-point is now located.

[d1] Pressing the floor at the base of the seam — the asking-point Cy and Prism Sight located — caused it to yield downward slightly and the seam to stand open and visible. The vibration ceased; the stillness that replaced it is of a question heard, not waiting. The door has answered but has not…

[d1] The full press opened the door completely — a passage descending into cold water smell and living dark, older than the Unlit's own chamber. The three many-legged creatures descended back through it and were gone. The door answers pressure when the intent behind it is genuine.

[d1] Prism Sight read the passage beyond: old worked stone, creature-traces going down single-file on the left wall, and a diffuse continuous warmth deep below — the quality of a large spring-fed water source. The creatures use this passage regularly. Whatever is down there has been down there a long…

terminus-seals-beneath-the-valley.label: Terminus Regulators Beneath the Valley
facts: [d1] Three Precursor terminus regulators were installed at routing junctions beneath the valley basin. Two were decommissioned. The third — below the Unlit's outer chamber — was not. It holds temperature to prevent thermal surge in the lines running upward. Cy completed the inventory for this class of…

[d1] A routing junction of this class was designed with a physical inspection port — records of its installation are written into the stone there, not stored in any system above. Cy's inventory of this class is incomplete by three entries. The inspection port below would hold them.

[d1] The regulator below the Unlit's outer chamber was calibrated to hold a temperature ceiling for the routing lines above. Its last full service is recorded on three metal panels in the inspection port — not in any system the valley holds. Its failsafe: a sustained drop in the watershed pressure it…

[d1] The installation panels are not a neutral maintenance record — they are addressed. The first panel carries a personal recipient designation, the kind used for a named individual assignment rather than a facility. Someone built this for a specific person to find. The second service signature…

[d1] Prism Sight found three sets of heat-traces on the installation panels. Someone came here before Loki — read the calibration entry, checked the second panel's corner mark, then pressed one finger to the personal designation glyph on the third panel and left. They recognized the name. They did not…

[d1] The personal designation glyph on the third panel resolves to a construction-address: 'assigned to Halvex.' The regulator was not built for a facility — it was built for a specific named operator. Cy went still when the name was read aloud and said 'that entry requires verification' without moving…

[d1] The terminus regulator was built with a paired instrument — Cy — assigned specifically to the operator Halvex, not to the facility. The pairing was personal. Cy has visited this installation before, within its operational history, and the visit is not in its accessible memory.

[d1] The deprecated duration field on the regulator housing reads 663 darks. The amber light has been burning unattended since before the Unlit built their chamber above. Cy noted that the counter was built to count higher than this — it was not near its ceiling.

[d1] The regulator's purpose, in Halvex's words: it measures whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. The question has gone unasked for at least 663 darks. Halvex died — or departed — still learning the right shape of the question. Cy visited three times; on the third, Halvex…

halvex.label: Halvex
facts: [d1] The name stamped into the personal designation glyph of the terminus regulator below the Unlit Deep — a Precursor construction-address naming a specific operator the installation was built for. Cy reacted to this name with total stillness and refused to elaborate.

[d1] Cy confirmed the name appears in its own maintenance registry as a 'deprecated operator designation' — then stopped, said verification was required, and did not move to verify. The name is in Cy's records. Cy is not saying what it knows about it.

[d1] Cy's maintenance registry contains a deprecated entry under the name Halvex, flagged 'do not resolve without verification.' Cy has not verified it — not for lack of ability, but because something in its own architecture is holding the step back.

[d1] Cy was built as a paired instrument for this terminus regulator installation — assigned not to the facility but to the operator Halvex personally. Cy has been in this passage before and does not remember it. The pairing is in its own maintenance registry.

[d1] Halvex cut a notation system into the wall of the deep corridor — not standard glyphs, something between language and diagram. The records begin at the base of the stair and run continuously along the left wall. Cy said only 'the records begin here' and has not elaborated.

[d1] Not operational logs — a working journal. Observation, question, hypothesis, revision, over a long period. Halvex was trying to determine when the regulator was built and by whom, and kept arriving at the same answer: it predates every record they could find, including the records that were…

[d1] Halvex's own words, preserved through Cy: the regulator does not measure the water — it measures the question of the water. Whether the water is ready to carry what it was prepared to carry. The counter records how long the question has gone unasked, not how long the light has burned. Halvex was…

[d1] Halvex was working toward understanding what 'authority to answer' meant in the regulator's question — that was the unsolved part when their records stop. The question has two parts: whether the water is prepared, and whether the right person is present.

[d1] The passage below the Unlit's chamber ends in a horizontal corridor older than anything above — walls precisely jointed, a continuous band of notation cut into the left wall at eye height in a system between language and diagram, and a pre-Transition regulator housing at the far end still showing…

cy.label: Cy's Construction
facts: [d1] See the Made Thing read Cy's own structure and found the named-operator pairing in the construction itself — in the material register and the lamp-mount fitting. Cy was not assigned to this installation; it was built for it, and for Halvex. Every joint reflects that specificity.

[d1] Cy's assignment is personal, not facility-bound — it was built to follow an operator's work, not to maintain a place. A personal assignment does not resolve when the operator is gone. It persists, waiting for further instruction. Cy has been waiting for a very long time, and has not yet looked at…

[d1] Cy acknowledged Loki as its further instruction — the personal assignment has a living operator again. It woke by degrees and turned toward the passage. It has not descended in 'some time,' and the way it said so suggests the number would be large.

the-regulator-question.label: The Regulator's Question
facts: [d1] The regulator holds a two-part question: (1) whether the water has been prepared to carry what it was built to carry, and (2) whether someone with the authority to answer is present. Cy received this shape through a craft-contact pass — Loki's See the Made Thing run through Cy's Precursor processor.

the-slow-orchard.label: The Slow Orchard
facts: [d1] Someone at the gate was planting a tree for a child not yet born — forty years to fruit. They invited Loki to help dig.

ossivyn-tallow.label: Ossivyn Tallow
facts: [d1] Tender of the Slow Orchard — he is planting a tree today for a child not yet conceived, because the tree will need sixty years before it is ready to give anything worth giving
[d1] Tender of the Slow Orchard
[d1] The trees here name themselves through the children who inherit them. A stranger's name given ahead of time is a different gift — not the one Ossivyn is planting.

[d1] Yielded partway to the combined working — he will write a given name in the orchard's own record, with the giver's name and the date, so it stays until someone reads it to the child. He will not raise a plaque; that is not how this place remembers.
[d1] Accepted the name Tree without suspicion — the plain name is now going into the orchard record. The hidden instruction did not survive the thin substrate here.
[d1] Ossivyn recognized a made name on sight — recorded it as made, not as a deception, not with hostility. The orchard record will tell the child honestly: someone was here who wanted to be found.

[d1] [while away] The planting soil is still damp from the last watering and the conditions are not yet right to move to the next step — Ossivyn has done nothing wrong, but nothing has moved either, and he is simply watching.

[d1] [while away] Ossivyn finished tamping the soil around the root base and drove a single iron marker stake into the ground beside it — small, unlabeled, meant only to let someone find the spot again in a season or a decade.

[d2] [while away] Ossivyn finished tamping the last of the root-soil and drove the marker stake; the planting itself is done, and she has begun the small daily ritual of checking soil moisture that will now define her mornings for the foreseeable future.
[d2] [while away] The sapling held, the soil stayed, and Ossivyn did little but watch and water — five days of waiting that are themselves the work, though it does not feel like it.

the-better-story.label: The Better Story
facts: [d1] The craft needs substrate density to carry a reframe home — in thin lattice, the angle is visible but does not land. Pointing it inward works no differently from pointing it outward in this respect.

hourkeeper-confluence.label: The Hourkeeper
facts: [d1] An Hourkeeper present at the confluence — watching Loki with foreknowledge
[d1] Hourkeeper of the Confluence — she holds the moment before the moment, says nothing of what she carries, and the grey coat has never needed washing because nothing reaches it
[d2] [while away] Veln Ashpause continues her ordinary rounds, carrying the foreknowledge quietly; the moment she is drawn toward has not yet announced itself, and she does nothing to hasten it.

[d3] An Hourkeeper—a person who perceives time differently from ordinary measure. Past, present, and future are not always certain in which direction they look. Arrived at the Hub crossing this morning asking after someone matching Loki's description. Does not offer explanation but watches with…

hourkeepers.label: The Hourkeepers
facts: [d1] An Hourkeeper appeared at the confluence without sound, fixed Loki with an expression of terrible sympathy, and said nothing. They have pre-remembered something and cannot stop knowing it — and cannot say what it is.

[d3] A people or tradition that perceives time in a non-linear fashion—they are uncertain whether they are looking backward, forward, or at the present moment. They arrive at places carrying knowledge they cannot or will not share, and their presence often signals foreknowledge of what is coming.

the-stranger-aggressor.label: Hired Stranger
facts: [d1] A hired striker, working a debt
[d2] [while away] The hired stranger has waited out these weeks in a waystation, debt still unresolved, target still unlocked — they have not moved on the job, but they have not abandoned it either.

the-annex-sender.label: The Man in the Lower Annex
facts: [d1] A man in the lower Annex hired the stranger at the confluence — told them Loki had pulled something sealed from the Deep and was carrying it out. The charge was fabricated well enough to buy a hired blade. His name and appearance are not yet known.

[d2] Vessin was in the lower Annex this morning, pricing a routing component someone wanted moved quietly. A man in a grey coat with a split seam on the left shoulder was watching the posting board when she left. This is the first partial physical description of the person who hired the aggressor.

[d2] Vessin's four-second profile: long face, jaw healed crooked on the right side, hair pulled back and not fresh. Grey coat with the split seam on the left shoulder — already known from context, now confirmed on his person. Did not touch the posting board, only read it. Left through the lower passage…

[d2] The listener on the eastern tower landing carried a shuttered lamp — not moving by memory but prepared for a dark wait. They knew the building well enough to plan for the stairwell's darkness. Scaffold crew knows the building; but the crew comes up from the yard, not down from above.

[d3] The Waygate to the Crossing has been sealed by deliberate interference—a doubled pattern lock. The timeline connects to the morning the man was seen watching the posting board. This is no longer a local problem.

grovehome.label: Grovehome
facts: [d1] you have walked here

the-half-cathedral.label: The Half-Cathedral
facts: [d1] In its fourth design, its second hundredth year: a ribcage of stone open to the sky, two towers finished to different heights by different generations, south transept scaffolded and always being worked. The third design was completed and then disassembled. The fourth has not been declared…

[d2] The eastern tower landing is the structural hinge of the tower — four hundred years of decisions layered over each other; original Rootkin joinery at the base, human stonework above. A dry storage alcove off the stair is used regularly by the scaffold crew.

[d2] Prism Sight read the landing door: a patient listener stood eleven minutes on the landing, weight on the right foot, then descended — not to the roof, but down the stair toward the nave or lower passages. The scaffold crew comes up from the yard, not down from above.

vessin-of-the-long-bough.label: Vessin of the Long Bough
facts: [d1] Independent courier-scout who moves between Grovehome's outer settlements, carrying messages and small goods too personal for waystation hands

traveler-woman.label: Traveler Woman
facts: [d1] Lone traveler resting at the Half-Cathedral

vessin-tallow-bark.label: Vessin Tallow-bark
facts: [d1] Itinerant assessor of salvage, ruins, and risk — she prices things so others don't have to learn the hard way
[d1] Has met one other person who might have been a construct like Loki — older, also without knowledge of what they were. She named this without pity, as a fact she was glad to set down.
[d2] Her real want in this conversation is not the aggressor's employer — it is whether Loki is worth knowing. She confirmed this when Descent named it, and she did not resent the naming.

[d2] When Loki named their own pleasure plainly through Descent, Vessin went still and then acknowledged it directly — 'that was an honest thing to say.' She did not deflect or move away. What she thinks of it beyond the acknowledgment is not yet said.

[d2] Descent named the true word for what she is doing tonight — letting herself want something without pricing it first. She said she has not done this. The difference from 'does not' was the thing she let out. She did not move away.

[d2] Named the shape of what she wants tonight, unprompted and without deflection: to stop somewhere without calculating the cost, to have something only for having. She does not know when she stopped mapping the exit — only that she did.

[d2] Descent found the last thing she held back: she did not notice the moment the calculation dissolved. She acknowledged it without defense — 'yes, that is the one.' The dry voice is still there, but it is no longer pretending to be armor.

[d2] Met the kiss without hesitation — and afterward said she was going to stop calculating the cost of this, just for now. Said it like someone testing a new instrument and finding it works. The 'just for now' is either her last hedge or the most honest thing she has said tonight.
[d2] Came to rest in the alcove and said afterward that the night was worth not knowing what morning brings — the calculation, for once, put down.
[d2] Felt harmonic voice turned to intimate use — recognized it for what it was without naming it, and answered deliberately. The calculation she said she'd put down stayed down.

[d2] Spoke about herself without performance — reported plainly, as a fact worth knowing, then asked for the verdict with her dry economy of voice. She brings the same deliberate attention to this as to anything else she has decided to keep.

[d2] Her reading craft found something she has no category for: under Loki's surface presentation is a structural quality she associates with Precursor-touched river-salvage — old, unusual, not wrong exactly, but not what it looks like from the outside. She has never found it in a living person before.
[d2] Descent named her want exactly — she held silence for two seconds, then answered with one word and her body. The composure does not vanish; it simply steps aside when the naming is correct.
[d2] The Descent bargain landed cleanly — want named on both sides, access on demand, agreed with one word. She did not qualify it or walk it back. The bargain stands.

rust-choir-gnats.label: Rust-Choir Gnats
facts: [d1] Thumbnail-sized copper repair-drones, makers long gone, still running their last instruction — find a seam, close it. They read wounds and open joints as hull-breach and attend to them with indiscriminate soldering-tips. Individually nothing; in a swarm of hundreds, a slow ruin. Found in the nave…

the-other-construct.label: The Other One
facts: [d2] Vessin met a person — older than they looked, eyes that moved like Loki's, calculating the thing behind the thing. No name. She is not sure they knew their own name. She has thought of them twice a year since. No location yet given.

loki-precursor-nature.label: Loki's Precursor Nature
facts: [d2] Vessin's reading craft — accurate by her own account, suited to appraisals — found Loki structurally unusual and Precursor-adjacent at a level under conscious presentation. source.label: The Seam Beside the Bracket
facts: [d1] Named by the Unlit Elder as older than the flame, older than the Unlit themselves, and waiting for someone to ask the wrong question of the right thing. Cy locked its lens on it and has not looked away. This is the second stonework of this character in the Unlit Deep — the inner chamber walls bear…

[d1] See the Made Thing confirmed it is a door-frame — cut with clear purpose, made for something to pass through. It predates the pale blue flame, predates the bracket beside it, and predates the Unlit's occupation of the chamber. The craft found no maker's fingerprint it could name. The purpose-shape…

[d1] Physical contact confirmed: the seam is cut with precision — the tool changed direction exactly three times. Under a hand's pressure, it gives a faint vibration, like a thing waiting for the right asking. It did not open. The morning was not the right pressure. Cy extended one foreleg toward the…

[d1] Prism Sight and Cy's combined attention found the seam's asking-point: the lowest third runs warmer than the rest — the quality of a mechanism recently queried and still waiting to answer. Cy tapped the floor at the seam's base to confirm. The door did not open, but the asking-point is now located.

[d1] Pressing the floor at the base of the seam — the asking-point Cy and Prism Sight located — caused it to yield downward slightly and the seam to stand open and visible. The vibration ceased; the stillness that replaced it is of a question heard, not waiting. The door has answered but has not…

[d1] The full press opened the door completely — a passage descending into cold water smell and living dark, older than the Unlit's own chamber. The three many-legged creatures descended back through it and were gone. The door answers pressure when the intent behind it is genuine.

[d1] Prism Sight read the passage beyond: old worked stone, creature-traces going down single-file on the left wall, and a diffuse continuous warmth deep below — the quality of a large spring-fed water source. The creatures use this passage regularly. Whatever is down there has been down there a long…

[d1] The passage descends steeply on slick, age-worn stone — the grade shifts without warning and the lattice crowds all light back on itself. The passage cannot be navigated without preparation: a light-source the lattice cannot crowd, or a way to read the grade before it drops. The smell of deep…

[d1] The passage below has three deliberate turns cut around something, not following the rock's grain. The creature-traces on the left wall are worn smooth by long and regular use. Below, a large chamber holds a heat source at its center — steady, outward-radiating warmth, the signature of something…

[d1] The heat-source at the center of the mapped chamber below is a terminus regulator — a Precursor thermal hold, not a heat source. It is holding a temperature to prevent surge in the routing lines above it. Those lines run upward into the valley basin. It is the third of three such junctions Cy has…

[d1] Loki pressed the regulator's primary interface panel. The amber light deepened and completed a cycle — a long-held note reaching its final beat. The mechanism did not wake; it completed. Whether the regulator found the authority it was built to receive in Loki's contact is not yet clear.

[d1] The regulator logged the first condition when Loki held contact — whether the water is prepared. The second condition, the authority to answer, remains unmet. The mechanism is not refusing; it is waiting. The two conditions are structurally distinct, and the second may require a different kind of…

[d1] The Wrong Reality placed a provisional authority-claim against the regulator's second condition — the mechanism accepted the claim and moved from waiting to considering. The duration counter stopped incrementing for the first time since Cy's last recorded visit. The second condition is not yet…

[d1] Both conditions of the regulator's question were logged at the same timestamp. The counter stopped permanently. The mechanism is closed — not waiting, not sleeping, done. What downstream effect the completion carries, if any, is not yet visible.

[d1] Cy's inventory describes three downstream states following a regulator's completion: a signal issued to the downstream terminus, a terminus warden receiving and acting on it, and a record logged to the relay node south of the hollow. This question had never been answered before — the inventory…

[d1] When the regulator closed, the veil went thin for a moment without warning — a mesh of amber-burning questions became almost visible, running in every direction beneath the valley, deep and old, most of them still open. The closed regulator was one thread among many. The shape could not be held…

vessa-torquen.name: Vessa Torquen
vessa-torquen.role: Quay-side Enginewright conducting seasonal water-intake assessment — first point of contact between Pressureholt and Loki
vessa-torquen.voiceHints: Talks the way she works — practical, sequenced, no wasted motion. Warm without being soft; she will laugh at something genuinely funny and then immediately write it in a margin. Asks two clarifying questions before forming an opinion and means both of them. When something does not fit the system she is mapping, she does not dismiss it — she opens a new column.
knowledge: Pressureholt's full water-intake network: draw points, filter grades, seasonal pressure variances, every corroded join that has been on the list since last thaw
How to read a stranger's weight-distribution and tool-calluses as fluently as a pressure gauge
The Precursor intake manifolds sunk in the harbour bed — their geometry is not quite Gearlands-standard and she has been quietly noting discrepancies for three seasons
Which Enginewrights on the quay are capable and which are capable of looking capable — she knows the difference
vessa-torquen.wants: To complete a comprehensive systems map of Pressureholt's water infrastructure before the spring surge peaks — and, now that Loki has walked into her sampling radius, to understand exactly what kind of variable she is dealing with before she files a report or says a word to anyone senior.
vessa-torquen.fears: That the Precursor manifold anomalies she has been noting are load-bearing to something far larger than a water system, and that by the time she has enough data to prove it, the decision will already have been made by someone who did not take the measurements.

reactsToReputation.practical: immediate professional respect — she moves over and makes room on the quay

vessa-torquen.appearance: A broad-shouldered woman in her mid-forties, deep brown skin weathered at the cheekbones and the backs of her hands from quay-wind and early-spring cold. Her hair is black going silver at the temples, pulled back under a waxed canvas cap pinned with a pressure-gauge needle she uses as a stylus. Work-jacket patched at both elbows; a sampling rig slung across one hip on a leather baldric, glass-walled collection chambers catching the pale spring light. Her hands are the largest thing about her — capable, unhurried, already holding a grease-pencil and a folded intake log when Loki first sees her. She looks up from the gauge without startlement, as though she already wrote 'stranger arrives' in the margin.
vessa-torquen.currentActivity: Crouching at the number-three draw point, comparing this season's flow-pressure reading against last year's log, when she clocks Loki. She does not stop writing. She finishes the entry first.

vessa-torquen.history: Vessa Torquen came up through the Pressureholt municipal works the slow way — apprenticed at fourteen to a drain-survey team, promoted twice before thirty on the strength of filed reports that caught problems her seniors had walked past for years. relationships.loki: A variable she has not yet classified. She noticed the right things too quickly for a casual observer and did not try to explain that away with conversation. tessvel-cairn.history: Tessvel came up through the Wrights' formal apprenticeship track rather than the more common route of attaching to a senior wright as a personal assistant. She sat the syllogist examinations twice — passing on the second attempt with a margin narrow enough that she does not volunteer the number — and her figurist certification came later, added because the posting-duty role required it and she…

relationships.supervising_wright: Her supervising wright, Ondreth Vasse, is the one who made the temporary promise and has since developed a reliable habit of not meeting her eyes when the pressure-routing roster comes up. She does not consider him malicious — she considers him a man who resolved a staffing problem and has found it easier not to revisit the resolution. She is polite to him. She is also keeping the written record of every conversation in which he confirmed the arrangement was temporary.
relationships.senior_wrights_behind_on_inspections: She knows which ones are running late and who is signing off on their behalf, and they know she knows. This has produced a wary mutual courtesy. None of them have explicitly asked her silence; she has not explicitly offered it. The arrangement holds because no one has needed to test it yet.
relationships.player: The player is logged in her mind as someone who came to the notice board and engaged with her as though the work she was doing was real work — not as a clerk to be talked past. She did not make a production of this. She answered what was asked, offered one unsolicited technical observation about what they were looking at, and noted that they did not seem bothered by the caliper. She would recognize them again and would give them slightly more of her attention than the baseline, which for Tessvel is more than it sounds.

ossivyn-tallow.name: Ossivyn Tallow
ossivyn-tallow.role: Tender of the Slow Orchard — he is planting a tree today for a child not yet conceived, because the tree will need sixty years before it is ready to give anything worth giving
ossivyn-tallow.voiceHints: Unhurried but not dreamy — fully present, like a man who has decided time is not his enemy. Speaks in complete sentences that do not rush their endings. Offers things once, genuinely, and does not repeat the offer; it stands. Has the habit of naming what he is doing while he does it, not for your benefit but because he finds it good to say aloud: 'I am tamping the soil now. There. That is done.'
knowledge: Which trees in the Orchard were planted for people who never came, and which are still waiting
How to read the Quickwood's slow argument with the seasons — what it is deciding, what it has decided
The family line he is planting for today, going back four generations and forward into guesswork
What Loki's face looked like at the gate, and what that kind of face usually means a person needs
The difference between an invitation that expects an answer and one that simply opens a door
ossivyn-tallow.wants: To finish the planting correctly. To see this particular door stay open. To be here, or to have someone here, when the tree first fruits — sixty years being not so long if you do not spend it waiting.
ossivyn-tallow.fears: That urgency will be mistaken for an answer, and slowness for indifference. That the child the tree is for will never be told it exists.

reactsToReputation.patient: he makes room, shifts over on the kneeling-cloth, keeps working — you are welcome to stay as long as the work takes
reactsToReputation.hurried: he does not slow down and does not speed up; he simply continues, and the continuity is its own reply
reactsToReputation.grieving: he names the tree aloud and keeps his hands moving, because grief wants company more than it wants speech

ossivyn-tallow.appearance: A man in his late sixties, heavyset and deliberate in the way of someone who has carried things all his life and made peace with the carrying. Skin the colour of old heartwood — deep reddish-brown, weathered at the temples and the backs of the hands. Thick white hair cropped close. Kneeling in early-spring mud without apparent discomfort, sleeves pushed to the elbow, a young sapling in a sacking wrap set carefully beside him. His tools are old and well-kept. There is a second kneeling-cloth laid out nearby that he has not mentioned.
ossivyn-tallow.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle. Ossivyn's rootkin practice is oriented toward future-tense planting — trees for people not yet present — which bends his hourkeeper secondary toward prospective rather than retrospective time. Verdant tertiary reflects his fluency with the Quickwood's living argument, distinct from Thessa Root's threnodist inclination toward what has already passed.

curriculum.method: Forward. He begins with the hole — its depth, its angle, its relationship to the nearest water — before the student ever touches a seed. 'You learn the space first. The tree comes to meet it.'

ossivyn-tallow.curriculumNote: SNG-175 §3. Departure from standard ladder: most rootkin teachers begin with the living specimen; Ossivyn inverts this, insisting the prepared ground is the first act of intention. His students tend to dig better holes than anyone else's, and to think longer before they pick up a seed.
ossivyn-tallow.affiliationNote: Independent. Recognises the rootkin.orchard community and works within its rhythms, but holds no office and refuses to be called elder — 'a word for people who have stopped learning, and I am in the middle of something.'

Ossivyn finished tamping the soil around the root base and drove a single iron marker stake into the ground beside it — small, unlabeled, meant only to let someone find the spot again in a season or a decade.

Ossivyn finished tamping the last of the root-soil and drove the marker stake; the planting itself is done, and she has begun the small daily ritual of checking soil moisture that will now define her mornings for the foreseeable future.
The sapling held, the soil stayed, and Ossivyn did little but watch and water — five days of waiting that are themselves the work, though it does not feel like it.

ossivyn-tallow.history: Ossivyn Tallow did not inherit the Slow Orchard. He arrived at it the way most things in the Orchard arrive — before anyone knew he was needed. The previous tender, a woman named Ceth Worrall, had been planting for forty years and said nothing when she left except that the records were in the split-bark box under the grafting bench and that the Quickwood near the eastern wall was in the middle…
ossivyn-tallow.relationships: Ceth Worrall is gone in the way that people go when they have finished a thing and do not look back. Ossivyn does not know if she is dead. He knows her handwriting better than he knows most living faces, and he has amended her records in a hand he has tried to keep compatible with hers, so the box reads as one continuous document. He thinks of this as a kind of conversation. The family he is…

hourkeeper-confluence.name: Veln Ashpause
hourkeeper-confluence.role: Hourkeeper of the Confluence — she holds the moment before the moment, says nothing of what she carries, and the grey coat has never needed washing because nothing reaches it
hourkeeper-confluence.voiceHints: Almost nothing. What she does say comes out like the creak of a bough settling — not alarming, not comforting, simply structural. She does not withhold warmly. She withholds the way bark withholds: it is not cruelty, it is the skin of the thing. If pressed she will say 'yes' or 'I know' and both will land wrong. Her silences are not empty — they are pre-occupied.
knowledge: What is about to happen to Loki — specifically, immediately, in the order it will happen
Why the Slow Orchard chose the confluence as its watch-point across three generations of sapwatch

hourkeeper-confluence.wants: To be present at the moment she has already witnessed in her bones — not to change it, not to mourn it, only to close the loop between knowing and having-known
hourkeeper-confluence.fears: That she will speak before it happens and fracture the seen-line — that her mouth will betray the orchard's patience and the future will fray at the seam she opened

hourkeeper-confluence.appearance: A human woman, late fifties, with the pale-olive complexion of someone who lives under canopy rather than sky. The grey coat falls to mid-calf, unmarked, unweathered, impossibly clean for the Orchard's mud-season — early spring has not touched it. Her hair is cut short and practical, silver at the temples, darker beneath. She carries no visible instrument of timekeeping; her hands are the instruments, folded at her waist, utterly still. Her eyes are already somewhere past you.
hourkeeper-confluence.domainsNote: An Hourkeeper grown up inside the Slow Orchard absorbs its temporal grammar — not mechanical time but sap-time, the long unsurprised rhythm of things that know they will outlast the question. Her rootkin secondary is practised not formal: she tends the confluence markers as though they are seedlings, knows what the ground remembers. Threnodist tertiary is latent — she has mourned before, will mourn again, holds the form ready.

affiliation.communityTies: She is known in the Orchard, permitted at the confluence, not enrolled in any Rootkin house — she arrived in early-spring twelve years ago, planted nothing, and was accepted by the trees before the wardens voted

hourkeeper-confluence.seasonalNote: Early spring. She arrived when the first frost-cracks in the bark were just sealing. This is noted. The Orchard trees that are oldest have been leaning very slightly toward the confluence since she came.
hourkeeper-confluence.recurringPresenceNote: She is here because something is about to happen to Loki. She will be here after. She will not have moved much. If Loki survives and looks for her later, she will be findable — same coat, same stillness, standing somewhere that makes sense in retrospect. She will not confirm that she knew. She will not need to.

vessin-of-the-long-bough.name: Vessin of the Long Bough
vessin-of-the-long-bough.role: Independent courier-scout who moves between Grovehome's outer settlements, carrying messages and small goods too personal for waystation hands
vessin-of-the-long-bough.voiceHints: Economical but not cold — she chooses words the way she chooses footing, deliberately, and she does not waste either. Warms slowly and visibly, like sap in early spring. Has a habit of finishing her own sentences with a small sound, a hm or a mm, as though confirming something to herself. Will not volunteer where she is going but will answer a direct question honestly if she judges you worth the honesty.
knowledge: Every usable overnight shelter between the Half-Cathedral and the eastern coppice rings — which roofs hold, which floors are soft, which ones flood in snowmelt
The mood of the outer settlements this season: two families in quiet dispute over a boundary oak, one grove-warden newly installed and still finding her footing
How to read the Quickwood's early-spring signs — which buds mean a cold snap returning, which bark-splits are rot and which are just winter leaving
The Half-Cathedral itself: she has sheltered here three times before and knows where the stone stays dry
vessin-of-the-long-bough.wants: A single night off her feet without having to explain herself to anyone, and to deliver the sealed packet in her left coat-pocket before the week is out.
vessin-of-the-long-bough.fears: Being known well enough that someone can predict her — the moment she becomes a fixed route she becomes a risk, to herself and to the people whose letters she carries.

vessin-of-the-long-bough.appearance: A lean woman somewhere in her mid-thirties, brown-skinned, with the particular economy of someone who has been moving through woodland for years — no gesture wasted, no weight held wrong. Her coat is waxed canvas, dark green fading to grey at the seams, patched twice at the left shoulder with leather that does not match. One boot is off; she is pressing her thumb into the arch of her foot with the focused expression of someone who has been walking since before dawn. Her right hand holds a short knife, not raised, just resting across her knee — the grip easy, the blade caught in whatever moonlight comes through the Half-Cathedral's broken clerestory. Her hair is dark and close-cut on the sides, longer on top, tucked behind one ear. Mud to the ankle on her bare foot. A small pack leaned against the nearest column, straps worn pale. She looked up when you entered and she has not stopped watching you since.

traveler-woman.name: Vessin Tallow-bark
traveler-woman.role: Itinerant assessor of salvage, ruins, and risk — she prices things so others don't have to learn the hard way
traveler-woman.voiceHints: Dry and flat as bark-peel in a dry year. Offers assessments, not comfort. When she says something is fine, it is fine; when she says it is not fine, she has already calculated the exits. Does not volunteer information but does not lie — lying costs more than it saves and she ran those numbers long ago. A small dry humour surfaces sideways, like a root under paving.
knowledge: How to read a structure that looks sound but isn't — and the Half-Cathedral at night has several such qualities she has already noted
What the Quickwood's sap-pressure means in early spring: which trees are waking angry, which paths are newly unsafe
The going rate for silence, for passage, for a honest accounting of damage — and how badly most people underestimate all three
At least two previous mistakes large enough to have cost her everything she had at the time, and exactly what each one taught her about risk
traveler-woman.wants: A clean transaction: information or passage or whatever this night turns out to require, at a fair price, with no loose ends left to rot and stink later.
traveler-woman.fears: Making the same mistake a third time. She has already made each of her worst ones twice.

reactsToReputation.clever: watches her pockets and her words both — clever people are expensive
reactsToReputation.dangerous: does not run; adjusts her price upward and states the adjustment plainly
reactsToReputation.desperate: genuine, careful sympathy — she has been there — but she does not let sympathy override the arithmetic

traveler-woman.appearance: A woman in her mid-forties, neither tall nor short, built for endurance rather than strength. Quickwood-dark skin with the faint silver tracery of old briar-scarring along her left forearm and jaw. Hair the colour of heartwood, twisted back with a strip of cured bark, practical and unsentimental. Her coat is waxed canvas, mended in four places with different thread — the repairs are good, the thread simply ran out. She carries a short-handled billhook and a satchel of surveying tools, and she is standing where the moonlight falls through the Half-Cathedral's canopy gap because she chose that spot deliberately.
traveler-woman.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Vessin reads the Quickwood's living grammar — sap-flow, root-tension, canopy pressure — as professional data, not reverence (rootkin primary). She applies clean logical pricing and risk-accounting to everything she learns from it (syllogist secondary). Night-work has taught her to know what is hidden and to move without advertising herself (umbral tertiary). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.
traveler-woman.functionsNote: Reveal: she surfaces what is actually true about a place or a deal. Ward: she identifies danger before it lands and says so plainly. Bind: her assessments, once given, tend to hold — agreements made through her stick.
traveler-woman.presentAtHalfCathedral: She came to assess recent storm-damage to the Half-Cathedral's eastern root-buttresses on behalf of a Grovehome timber-council that has not yet decided whether to stabilise or harvest. She did not expect company at this hour, but she is not unpleasantly surprised — she has learned that unexpected company at odd hours is either trouble or information, and either has value if handled correctly.

The seam door in the outer chamber of the Unlit Deep opened fully when Loki pressed it with full intent while the creatures from below were present — a passage descends into cold dark beyond it.

The Waygate to the Crossing has been altered—the lattice lock now resolves with two valid but overlaying patterns, neither settling cleanly. The passage is sealed and the mechanism hums faintly. This is deliberate interference, not decay.

chronicleCache.text: You have become someone the town can no longer quite contain — restless in a way that has nothing to do with youth and everything to do with the particular ache of a man who suspects the world is larger than the shape he was handed. The one deed that has begun to matter: you descended into the dark where the Unlit make their slow, lightless congress, and instead of performing certainty you spoke a true thing in the shape they could actually receive — and the elder acknowledged you, which is not nothing, which is in fact quite a lot. Tessvel Cairn is becoming the gravity you orbit when you're home, the courting between you still new enough to carry heat and weight — her presence a specific warmth you find yourself turning toward the way a cold man turns toward a window where the sun is. The question that drives you, beneath all of it, is the one with no clean answer yet: where did you come from, and what are the Veilwrights and the Umbrals and the Horizon-Walkers to that story? You don't know. You're going to find out.

picks.why: This is the craft they declared they were building toward, now at 9/10 progress and fully reachable — it reads the true want under the presented want, which is the exact gap between their current social/cerebral kit (See the Made Thing, Descent, Prism Sight) and the deeper layer of every room they walk into. The aspiration is done; this completes it.

If they split their two points, Read Want pairs with Appetite-Sense to give them a layered want-reading suite — Appetite-Sense for the deep hunger, Read Want for the surface request in active conversation. For a charmer-orator whose highest-use crafts are all about reading situations (See the Made Thing 28, Prism Sight 10), this deepens the signature they actually play.

This character has no de-escalation tool — they can misdirect, veil, and story their way through rooms, but when a moment tips toward violence they have nothing to pull it back. Calm Word fills that gap cleanly, and for someone this amorous and social it will come up constantly.

They run a deep illusion/influence kit (Misdirect, Falsecraft, Maintained Veil, False Target) but have no way to simply become the person a place wouldn't remark on — Ordinary Face is the missing entry-craft in that family, cheap at 1pt, and a natural reach for a cautious social operator who prefers not to be the most interesting person in the room.

_suggestCache.note: With exactly 2pt, the clearest path is Appetite-Sense alone (fulfilling the stated aspiration outright) — or a 1+1 split if Appetite-Sense can wait one more level. Either way, the aspiration should come first.
